knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A bouncing board and a stain that may be water are structural or suspect defects. They are referred and recorded, not filled or hidden.
A small surface gap is cosmetic when the approved scope allows it. Subfloor sag, rot and water damage are structural or suspect.
The filler colour and finish are tested on an offcut before the filler is used on the floor.
A suspect adhesive joint is assessed under NEW-TMB-03 before any cutting, grinding or filling.
Sanding filler produces airborne dust, so the same extraction controls as sanding apply.

practicalCriteria: Candidate maps at least four defects on a sample floor and classifies each as cosmetic, structural or suspect.
Candidate refers a structural or water-related defect on the mock-up and records the referral with photos and location.
Candidate tests filler colour on an offcut, and fills one cosmetic gap in scope, then re-checks under raking light.
passRule: Knowledge checks: at least 80% correct (4 of 5). Practical sign-off is separate. A knowledge pass does not establish practical competence, and the practical criteria must be observed and recorded by an assessor.
evidenceRequired: Defect map with classification and photos
Referral record for structural or water-related defects
Filler colour test record and repair record
stopWorkCriteria: Structural defect repaired under this course
Stain filled without finding its cause
Filler applied over a suspect adhesive joint without assessment
